blocks.text: Debug networking from inside the caller's network namespace: check network membership, then use a tool container that shares the namespace, or nsenter, when the image has no tools.

$ docker network inspect rag_default --format '{{range .Containers}}{{.Name}} {{.IPv4Address}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}'
$ docker inspect -f '{{json .NetworkSettings.Networks}}' rag-api-1 | jq 'keys'
Same network? That alone settles most DNS failures.
2. From the caller, with no extra tools

$ docker compose exec api getent hosts db
$ docker compose exec api python -c "import socket; print(socket.create_connection(('db',5432),3))"

$ docker run --rm -it --network container:rag-api-1 nicolaka/netshoot
~ # dig db ; nc -vz db 5432 ; ss -ltnp ; tcpdump -i eth0 port 5432 -nn
`--network container:<name>` = same IP, same localhost, same DNS as the app. `--network rag_default` joins as a new peer instead.

$ PID=$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Pid}}' rag-api-1)
$ sudo nsenter -t "$PID" -n ss -ltnp
LISTEN 0 2048 127.0.0.1:8000     # bug: bound to loopback
Uses host binaries, so it works with distroless images.

Q: "How do you debug networking in a container that has no shell or tools?" A: "Attach nicolaka/netshoot with --network container:<name> to share its exact namespace, or nsenter -n from the host using the container's PID, then resolve, connect and check listeners with ss."

items: Python or /dev/tcp can replace missing tools.
